subject: ACME dedicated capacity onboarding — sizing & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for pilot

Marcus / Hannah / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ACME wants to move a small Dedicated capacity pilot ahead (Q3 target). Before legal and procurement start, procurement asked for: 1) a sizing estimate for 3 months based on our expected workload, 2) a realistic hardware lead time if we go with Reserved (OEM + cloud reserved instances), and 3) a short list of vendor contacts for quotes.

I've attached a simple workload projection (ACME-expected-workload.csv) with peak concurrent requests, 99p token lengths, and inferred batchability. We expect ~250k prompt tokens/day ramping to 1.2M by week 8. We are targeting latency 95p < 350ms for completion on chat flows.

Can you send a short one-pager with: recommended Dedicated capacity (GPU types / instance counts), expected procurement lead time options (OEM build vs cloud reserved vs hybrid), and any quick mitigations (quantization, prefix caching, burst strategies) that would change the lead time or cost?

If helpful, cc'ing FastCloud and Titan contacts to loop them into procurement questions.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of ML Platform, ACME Corp

Attachment: ACME-expected-workload.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for pilot

Samantha — thanks for the projection and the clear ask. Looping Dev for sizing and to get an OEM/cloud timeline.

High level for procurement to digest:
- Short answer: for your projected 1.2M tokens/day with 95p latency target, we recommend starting with a mixed pool: 4x A800-class GPUs (reserved) for steady throughput + 2x smaller accelerator instances for burst (or equivalently 6x A100-80GB if you prefer single SKU).
- Opt-in mitigations that shorten procurement pressure: aggressive 4-bit quantization and prefix KV caching can drop reqs by ~30% token-cost/throughput, often letting you start with 20–30% fewer GPUs for the pilot.
- Lead time: cloud reserved instances (FastCloud) can be provisioned ~2–4 weeks depending on region and quota; OEM bare-metal/onsite procurement typically runs 8–12+ weeks from PO to delivery (longer if custom builds).

I'll have Dev add a more detailed estimate (p95 latency vs concurrency) and attach existing vendor availability notes.

Next steps: Dev will produce a short SOW-ish sizing summary, and Hannah/Karthik can push this into procurement + we can get vendor quotes.

— Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity ask for pilot

Marcus / Samantha — dug into the CSV. Quick technical sketch and options (attaching vendor availability sheet):

Option A — Fast start (cloud reserved / hybrid)- Configuration: 6x rA800 (shared in a dedicated pool)- Expected throughput: ~1.5–2.0M tokens/day headroom for model sizes in your evals- Procurement lead time: 2–4 weeks to spin up reserved capacity (subject to region quota)- Upside: fastest time-to-live, simpler network/security integration- Downside: higher unit cost vs raw OEM bare-metal

Option B — OEM bare-metal (longer runway, lower unit cost)- Configuration: 6x A100-80GB class nodes (OEM supplied / rack-ready)- Expected throughput: similar to Option A once tuned- Lead time: 8–12 weeks typical; 14+ if GPU supply tight or special QC requested- Upside: lower ongoing cost, full control, easier for on-prem/VPC variants

Option C — Staged buy (recommended for deals with >12 month horizon)- Start: 3x reserved A800 + heavy caching and quantization for pilot (1–2 weeks)- Follow with: OEM order for 6–8 nodes with 10–12 week lead; transition capacity over 3 months- Procurement cadence: short-term cloud contract + PO for OEM with staggered delivery

Mitigations/notes:
- If ACME accepts 4-bit quantization and a small policy to route non-latency-critical workloads to cheaper instances, you can cut required peak GPUs by ~25–35%.
- We can provide a short config.json for your infra team to validate NICs / NVLink / kernel deps for OEM installs.
- FastCloud availability sheet attached: FastCloud-availability-2026Q3.xlsx

Attachment: FastCloud-availability-2026Q3.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)

Let me know if you want me to ping Titan for a formal quote or run a short load test on our hosted infra to validate latency assumptions.
— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: Titan GPU Sales <oem-quote@titan-gpu.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Titan preliminary quote attached

Marcus / Dev / Samantha — attaching a preliminary OEM quote (Titan-quote-0426.pdf). High level: we can commit to a 10–12 week build window for a 6-node A100-80GB rack in NA, or 14 weeks if certain supply items (NVLink bridges) are delayed. We can expedite to 8 weeks with a 12% expedite surcharge and prepayment on critical components.

Please note these windows are impacted by ongoing supplier backlogs; confirm quantity and any custom NICs now to lock lead times.

Regards,
Rajesh Kumar
Enterprise Sales, Titan GPU
oem-quote@titan-gpu.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME dedicated capacity onboarding — sizing & procurement timeline

Samantha — quick note from procurement side and timeline suggestion:

We usually see legal + procurement take 2–3 weeks for NDA + SOW for pilots. To align timelines for a Q3 pilot start, suggested action items:
1) ACME to confirm preferred option (A/B/C) and sign the pilot SOW (I can share a templated SOW by EOD).
2) If choosing OEM (Option B or C) open an RFQ with Titan this week and request the expedited option if you need <10 week delivery.
3) If choosing cloud reserved, I'll engage FastCloud and get formal quota confirmation — they indicated region quotas are tight in us-west-2 for A800-class but can often meet 2–3 week spin-up if we have account-level approval.

I'll attach a one-page procurement checklist for your team once you confirm option.

— Karthik
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 22:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: ACME dedicated capacity onboarding — sizing & procurement timeline

Samantha — following up with a concise next-steps pack (below) so procurement can move quickly. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to run through the checklist and confirm which option to pursue.

One-page recommended plan (actionable):
- If ACME needs pilot live within 4 weeks: choose Option A (FastCloud reserved) + enable quantization and KV caching; I will have Karthik secure quota and Dev will provision. Target: PO + account approval this week.
- If ACME prefers lower monthly cost and can accept a 10–12 week lead: choose Option B (OEM) and request Titan expedite with 12% surcharge — Karthik to start RFQ, Samantha to issue PO window.
- Recommended hybrid (Option C) if you want fastest time-to-live with long-term cost optimization: start cloud reserved immediately and place staggered OEM PO.

Attachments: Titan-quote-0426.pdf, FastCloud-availability-2026Q3.xlsx, ACME-expected-workload.csv

Please reply with chosen option and any procurement constraints (payment terms, PO lead time, need for audit/SOC docs). We can also produce a short cost delta table (monthly reserved vs OEM amortized) if helpful.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to procurement.
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
